nodes.question: What were the payback periods for the different heating methods evaluated in the study?
nodes.answer: The payback periods are 11 years for electric heating, 24 years for coal-fired heating, and 6 years for biomass heating.
nodes.paragraph: Study on indoor thermal environment and energy consumption of traditional dwellings of ethnic minorities in Sichuan plateau Yan Zhang1 & Biao Wang2,3 In this paper, field tests, questionnaire surveys, and DesignBuilder were used to analyse the indoor thermal environment and energy consumption of traditional houses in a traditional ethnic minority village of Western Sichuan Plateau of China, The results showed that during the summer test period, the outdoor temperature range was 9.37.8 C and the relative humidity range was 53.5 67.4%, while the indoor temperature range of the tested room was 13.3 2.3 C, and the relative humidity range was 69.1 83.0%. The humidity is high, and the thermal environment does not meet the requirement of local standard. Therefore, corresponding energy-saving optimization measures are proposed. In the winter heating building model data, compared with the heat load before optimization, the energy saving reaches about 56.5%. In addition, the carbon emissions and economic suitability of different heating methods were evaluated. Electric heating, coal-fired heating and biomass heating have payback periods of 11 years, 24 years and 6 years respectively.

nodes.question: What is one environmentally favorable alternative to combustion in CHP units?
nodes.answer: Upgrading to transport fuel such as biomethane is an environmentally favorable alternative to combustion in CHP units.
nodes.paragraph: (1234567890) combined heat and power production (CHP) in CHP units or can be purified into biomethane, which can be used in the gas grid for natural gas or in gas pow - ered vehicles (Hakawati et al. 2017; Scarlat et al. 2018). The upgrading to transport fuel offers an envi- ronmentally favorable alternative compared to com- bustion in CHP units (Styles et al. 2016). Nutrients in the organic input material are mostly retained in the residue after digestion, the digestate, which can be used as a bio-based fertilizer to recycle nutrients back to agricultural fields. The recent expansion of biogas production across Europe (Gustafsson & Anderberg 2022) has resulted in a lack of energy-rich feedstocks such as slaughterhouse waste. Potential supple- mentary feedstocks for biogas production which are receiving growing interest are cover crops (Feng et al. 2020). Cover crops are grown to reduce leaching of nutri- ents and soil erosion when there is no main crop in the field, i.e. in the time between main crops, mostly dur - ing autumn and winter.
